players.product: AI server and switch system integration

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO): revenue of $3.65 billion was up 44% and above the high end of guidance, driven by very strong CCS demand; non-GAAP operating margin 7.7% (up 90 basis points; the CEO called it the strongest performance in company history); adjusted EPS $1.89 (up 70%); adjusted gross margin 11.3%; adjusted ROIC 43%. CCS segment revenue was $2.86 billion, up 64% (78% of revenue), with communications up 79% on strong demand and ramping 800G networking switch programs across the largest hyperscaler customers, and enterprise up 33%; CCS segment margin 8.4%. HPS revenue was $1.4 billion, up 72% (38% of revenue), on ramping 800G switch programs with multiple hyperscaler customers. ATS revenue was $795 million, 1% lower. Three customers each accounted for at least 10% of Q4 revenue: 36%, 15% and 12%. Full-year 2025 (CEO): revenue of $12.4 billion and adjusted EPS of $6.05, growth of 28% and 56%, with adjusted operating margin of 7.5%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $3.65 billion (up 44%); adjusted EPS $1.89; operating margin 7.7%; CCS $2.86 billion (up 64%); HPS $1.4 billion (growth of 72%); Q4 10%+ customers 36%, 15%, 12%; FY2025 revenue $12.4 billion (28%)

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance (management): Q1 2026 revenue projected between $3.85 billion and $4.15 billion (growth of 51% at the midpoint), adjusted EPS between $1.95 and $2.15 (71% growth at the midpoint), non-GAAP operating margin expected at 7.8%. Q1 communications revenue expected to grow in the low sixties percentage range on ongoing ramps in multiple 800G programs with hyperscaler customers; ATS down in the low single digits. The FY2026 annual outlook was raised to revenue of $17 billion and adjusted EPS of $8.75 (year-over-year growth of 37% and 45%), with the free cash flow outlook maintained at $500 million after paying for a billion dollars of capex; CCS full-year revenue growth of approximately 50%; ATS approximately flat to up mid-single digits. The CFO said 'Our customer forecasts right now for 2026 are higher than the $17 billion that we are guiding', and management called the 30 basis points of 2026 margin expansion 'the floor of our expectations'. Longer range: three months earlier the company had implied about $3.5 billion of 2026 CCS growth and about $5 billion of CCS growth in 2027; now 2026 CCS 'will grow probably closer to $4.5 billion. So about a billion dollars higher than what we talked about three months ago', and 'we're now seeing CCS grow close to $7 billion in 2027', off a higher base and including the digital native customer's program. Customer visibility is 'unprecedented': 'We're totally into '27, and many customers were talking into 2028.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue $3.85 billion to $4.15 billion (51% at the midpoint); FY2026 revenue $17 billion, adjusted EPS $8.75 (37% and 45%); free cash flow $500 million; CCS growth closer to $4.5 billion in 2026 and close to $7 billion in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: New networking win (CEO): Celestica 'secured the design and manufacturing award for the 1.6T networking switch platform with a third hyperscaler customer'; this HPS engagement is expected to ramp production beginning in 2027, with design work already underway. With this hyperscaler Celestica held predominant share on 400G and on 800G; the 1.6T engagement started with a design win and Celestica was also awarded the mass production for the switch. Separately, mass production for the first 1.6T switching programs is expected to begin ramping in the latter part of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T switch design and manufacturing award with a third hyperscaler; production ramp beginning in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Switch generation cadence (management): Celestica has '10 active 1.6T programs in the pipeline right now'; about five of them start ramping in the back half of 2026 and into 2027, and several of the rest are in development and ramp later in '27 into '28. The gating factor is completing the development cycle as planned, and silicon is on track. 400G remains highly resilient and a strong 2026 contributor, 800G continues to grow, and 1.6T comes on toward the end of 2026: 'the next-generation technology is not necessarily cannibalizing the previous generation.' The 1.6T wins to date are used for both scale-up and scale-in. At 1.6T and 3.2T the engineering complexity is moving engagements toward HPS (design-led) work, and the CFO expects 1.6T programs to be as profitable as past switching programs. Some business Celestica declined to chase on price in 2025 came back in 2026 'because others could not execute on it.'
quarterly_data.figure: 10 active 1.6T programs; about five ramp in the back half of 2026; 400G, 800G and 1.6T running concurrently

quarterly_data.signal: Co-packaged optics and 3.2T (management): customer conversations on co-packaged optics are increasing, but 'in terms of mass adoption, it's going to be more towards 3.2T, which are programs that we're working on in our R&D group. But we haven't seen customers looking for mass adoption of CPO as of yet.' 3.2T switch samples are due probably towards the end of 2026 and work has already started; Celestica has proof-of-concept work on co-packaged optics so it is ready when CPO hits the 3.2T cycle. On scale-up, management sees increasing R&D activity toward fully integrated AI/ML and networking systems supporting both scale-up and scale-out fabrics: 'scale-up will be as much of an opportunity as scale-out.'
quarterly_data.figure: 3.2T samples towards the end of 2026; CPO mass adoption expected at 3.2T

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity build-out (management): after aligning long-term capacity plans with key CCS customers, Celestica expects 2026 capital expenditures of approximately $1 billion, or 6% of its current annual revenue outlook, fully funded from operating cash flow (Q4 2025 capex was $95 million, or 2.6% of revenue). Plans: over 700,000 square feet of added footprint with expanded power availability at the Richardson campus and a new site in Fort Worth, Texas, for R&D, manufacturing and advanced assembly (online in 2027); over 1 million square feet of added footprint in Thailand with expanded power availability, advanced liquid cooling manufacturing and testing (online towards the end of 2026 and into 2027); new manufacturing lines in locations such as Mexico and Japan; and new HPS Design Centers in Austin and Taiwan. The build-out 'is based on booked business' after 'a record bookings year in 2025' and enables capacity for 2027 and 2028; maintenance capex is probably $70 million to $80 million, and 'the vast majority of the expenditures are tied to programs with our hyperscalers.'
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex approximately $1 billion (6% of revenue outlook); Q4 capex $95 million; Texas over 700,000 square feet; Thailand over 1 million square feet

quarterly_data.signal: Supply and pricing (management): beyond the next two quarters the outlook is pragmatic while the company focuses on securing supply: 'We have no concerns at this time, but we just want to make sure that the supply base can also ramp as fast as we are ramping.' The CEO said 'Demand continues to well outstrip our ability to provide it in the very short term.' Inflation and pricing are factored into guidance: networking is built on a turnkey basis that includes the silicon, while compute typically does not; silicon price inflation is being passed on to customers with no margin compression at present, and a little of the year-over-year revenue growth comes from rising ASPs, but 'the vast majority of the growth is due to units.' Suppliers recognize Celestica's scale, and being a design agent gives it further leverage in the supply chain.

Digital native customer (unnamed on this call): the program 'continues to progress just as we would have expected it to' and is still expected to be a meaningful contribution in 2027. Celestica is actively working on the design aspects; in 2026 it will ship 'largely samples' ahead of a ramp 'that should be starting in the early parts of 2027', working with the customer, 'the silicon provider and all the ecosystem partners.' Some of the capex is going toward enabling that 2027 ramp. Management cited this engagement as a proof point for fully integrated AI/ML and networking rack systems supporting both scale-up and scale-out fabrics.
quarterly_data.figure: samples in 2026; ramp starting in the early parts of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Enterprise end market revenue was higher by 33% in Q4 2025, above guidance of a low twenties percentage increase, 'driven by the acceleration in the ramping of a next-generation AIML compute program with a large hyperscaler customer'. Management saw a meaningful ramp in that program during the quarter and expects volumes to accelerate into 2026, with the program growing all through 2026. On the compute side Celestica's revenue typically does not include the silicon (unlike turnkey networking), so silicon price inflation does not drive its enterprise growth. The enterprise mix shift is not expected to be a large margin headwind, although Celestica makes more money on networking in general.
quarterly_data.figure: enterprise revenue higher by 33% (guidance low twenties)

contracts.signal: CEO: 'As a preferred manufacturing partner for Google's Tensor Processing Unit, or TPU systems, Celestica is committed to making long-term investments in both capacity and capabilities both in the United States and across our global footprint', including the planned 2026 and 2027 capacity expansion, designed to support the scaling of production for 'current and future generations of Google's custom silicon TPU systems'. He described a decade-long partnership that 'has never been stronger or more integrated', with 'a joint commitment to each other moving forward, not just for the current generation but for future generations of their TPUs', and 'absolutely no indication there are new entrants into that market.' Celestica is not sole- or single-sourced on the TPU programs ('For BCP purposes, most, if not all, of our hyperscaler customers remain a second source'), 'But we are the primary source for them on the TPU programs'. The CFO expects TPU demand from adopters beyond Google to flow through Google's supply chain, which Celestica as preferred manufacturing partner expects to support.

quarterly_data.signal: Next-generation compute (management): Celestica has 'already won the next generation of that program' (the hyperscaler AI/ML compute program ramping through 2026) and expects those programs 'to actually ramp into 2027'. Looking towards 2027, management anticipates strong demand from hyperscaler and digital native customers driven by ramps in next-gen AI/ML compute programs; on the compute side Celestica focuses on HPS and JDM design-oriented work and has 'several projects in the pipeline to improve those engagements on the HPS side'.
quarterly_data.figure: next-generation program already won; ramp into 2027
